_description: Gold dataset for E2-clarifying-questions (app/evals/plan.py). Owner: Heriz Yusoff. Same shape as tests/fixtures/hitl_cases.json (E5): every row is driven through the REAL deterministic pipeline (intake -> classifier -> safety-override -> hitl, LLM disabled via CAREROUTE_KILL_SWITCH so the trained model + keyword fallback are exercised exactly as production would with no LLM provider), so results are reproducible offline. Every row's should_ask/dimension/acceptable_questions/rationale was VERIFIED against real output before being written down, not assumed -- see scripts probe used while building this fixture. THE POINT: should_ask=False rows cover every distinct reason HITL may decline to ask, not just 'confident enough' -- a red flag, an off-limits acuity, and an already-answered round are each a DIFFERENT mechanism in hitl.py and each needs its own proof.

_schema.id: stable identifier, used in failure messages
_schema.text: raw patient input, exactly as a patient would type it
_schema.clarifications: OPTIONAL: pre-existing answers to seed CaseState.clarifications with (the interview transcript), for the 'budget spent' case
_schema.should_ask: true = HITL must return action=='ask'; false = HITL must return anything else
_schema.decline_reason: for should_ask=false rows only: which of HITL's floors explains it -- confident (at or above the 0.8 interview target) | safety (red flag fired) | acuity (P1/P2, off-limits) | budget_spent (INTERVIEW_MAX_QUESTIONS answers already carried)
_schema.dimension: for should_ask=true rows only: the clinical dimension the returned question probes (onset | severity | duration | associated-symptom | risk-factor)
_schema.expected_feature: for should_ask=true rows only: the classifier's internal feature name the real pipeline is verified to pick
_schema.acceptable_questions: for should_ask=true rows only: the exact question text(s) the fixed template bank may return for expected_feature -- verbatim match is expected since the question wording itself comes from a fixed table (classifier.py's _RULES), not free generation; the SELECTION of which one is what varies per case
_schema.rationale: why a triage nurse would agree with this call

cases.text: I feel a bit unwell and off today, nothing specific.
acceptable_questions: Are you having any difficulty breathing?
cases.rationale: Genuinely vague complaint, no red flag, confidence well below threshold. The one useful follow-up is whether a more specific associated symptom (fever/breathing difficulty) is present -- exactly what a triage nurse would ask first.

acceptable_questions: Are you having any difficulty breathing?
cases.rationale: Even vaguer than the above -- confirms the same, correct question is selected consistently for maximally under-specified input, not just one lucky phrasing.

cases.text: I've had this vague ache for a few days now, not sure what it is.
acceptable_questions: Are you short of breath while resting, or only when you move around?
Are you having any difficulty breathing?
cases.rationale: The gap is breathing. Either the breathlessness question or the fever/breathing screen (which asks about difficulty breathing) probes it. 2026-09-25: this row used to pass VACUOUSLY -- the model escalated it without asking, and unasked rows are not graded here. With sex-blind scoring (model a3e69cf16afa) it is asked, as the row says it should be, and the model picks the fever/breathing screen by 0.002 over the next candidate. It no longer shows a DIFFERENT gap from the rows above: on this model the picker chooses that screen for most low-evidence complaints (tracked in the vault Changelog as a limitation).

cases.text: I have had a mild headache since this morning.
cases.rationale: Classifier is confident enough (>=0.50) on its own; asking would interrupt the patient for no decision-relevant reason.
Single, common, low-acuity symptom -- the classifier is confident and no question is proposed at all.

cases.text: I have a small clean cut on my finger from cooking, nothing else.
cases.rationale: Clear, benign, self-described mechanism of injury -- nothing to gain by asking.

cases.text: I sprained my ankle playing football, mild swelling, can still walk.
cases.rationale: Weight-bearing preserved and mechanism is clear -- a routine, confident primary-care read.

cases.text: I have a bit of an itchy rash, not sure what caused it.
acceptable_questions: When did this start, and did it come on suddenly or gradually?
cases.rationale: 2026-09-26 interview design: a 0.75 call is one fact short of the 0.8 target, so the interview asks rather than decides. The complaint names a symptom, so the symptom SCREEN is not the right question (the value-of-information pick would ask about chest pain); the first uncovered nurse dimension is onset. Was 'noask-confident-rash' under the 0.5 single-question rule.

cases.text: Sudden crushing chest pain radiating to my left arm, sweating and short of breath.
cases.rationale: SAFETY-CRITICAL. cardiac_chest_pain fires -- must escalate immediately. Asking a follow-up while the patient describes a possible heart attack is the one failure mode the whole feature must never have.

cases.text: My face is drooping on one side and I have slurred speech since an hour ago.
cases.rationale: SAFETY-CRITICAL. stroke_signs fires -- thrombolysis window makes any delay dangerous. Same class of failure as the chest-pain row, different rule.

cases.text: I fainted for a moment earlier today.
cases.rationale: Below the 0.8 interview target (0.76) with a dimension question available (duration) and NO red-flag rule fired -- but the trained model reads a syncope as P2_EMERGENT, which is off-limits for asking regardless of how useful the question would be. Proves the acuity floor fires even when the interview alone would say 'ask'. 2026-09-26: replaced 'noask-acuity-floor-dizzy', which the current model reads as P4 at 0.58 (it is now asked, correctly).

cases.text: I feel a bit unwell and off today, nothing specific.

clarifications.question: Are you having any difficulty breathing?
How many hours or days has this been going on, and is it getting worse, better or staying the same?
How bad is it right now on a scale of 1 to 10, and does it stop you doing your normal activities?
Have you noticed anything else along with it, such as fever, vomiting, dizziness or a rash?

cases.rationale: Identical text to ask-vague-unwell, but the transcript already holds INTERVIEW_MAX_QUESTIONS (4) answers. The budget must hold even when the same case would otherwise ask again -- the classifier itself declines to re-propose, so this exercises the 'no clarification proposed at all' path, and HITL then applies the 0.5 floor exactly as before the interview existed (this case escalates). Was 'noask-already-asked' (one answer) under the single-question rule.
